question.problem:
If ${X}_{1}∼N(8,{40}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N(30,{30}^{2})$ are independent and $Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2},$ calculate $P(-31\le Y\le 31).$ Round your final answer to two decimal places. *Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,-0.3\,$ $\,0.3557\,$ $\,0.3520\,$ $\,0.3483\,$
$\,-0.2\,$ $\,0.3936\,$ $\,0.3897\,$ $\,0.3859\,$
$\,-0.1\,$ $\,0.4325\,$ $\,0.4286\,$ $\,0.4247\,$
$z$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$
$\,0.9\,$ $\,0.8289\,$ $\,0.8315\,$ $\,0.8340\,$
$\,1.0\,$ $\,0.8531\,$ $\,0.8554\,$ $\,0.8577\,$
$\,1.1\,$ $\,0.8749\,$ $\,0.8770\,$ $\,0.8790\,$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2})$, and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2} & ∼N({\mu }_{1}-{\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(8-30,{40}^{2}+{30}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(-22,2500).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =-22$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{2500}=50.$ 

We want to find $P(-31\le Y\le 31).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-31\le Y\le 31) & =P(\frac{-31-(-22)}{50}\le Z\le \frac{31-(-22)}{50}) \\  & =P(-0.18\le Z\le 1.06) \\  & =P(Z<1.06)-P(Z<-0.18) \\  & =Φ(1.06)-Φ(-0.18)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.18) & ≈0.4286 \\ Φ(1.06) & ≈0.8554\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-31\le Y\le 31) & =Φ(1.06)-Φ(-0.18) \\  & ≈0.8554-0.4286 \\  & ≈0.43.\end{aligned}
$$
